n: Amos bluntly calls the wealthy women of Samaria “cows of Bashan” — well-fed and pampered. They demand drinks from their husbands while their luxury is funded by crushing the poor.

f.g: Kine = cows. Bashan, east of the Sea of Galilee, was famous for rich pasture and fat cattle.

n: God swears by His own holiness that they will be dragged away with hooks. Assyrian carvings show captives led by ropes attached to hooks.

f.g: The Hebrew may mean hooks or harpoons; the picture is of being hauled off helplessly.

n: They will be led out single file through holes broken in the city wall, each one straight ahead, and thrown out toward Harmon (the meaning of that place is uncertain).

f.g: Gaps knocked in the city wall by attackers.
Hebrew obscure; often read “cast out toward Harmon,” perhaps a place name.

n: With heavy sarcasm Amos mimics a priest: “Come to Bethel and sin! Go to Gilgal and sin even more!” Their busy religion at false shrines only adds to their guilt.

f.g: Or “every three days” — mocking their over-eager, showy devotion.

n: They love to show off their offerings and announce their generosity. Their worship is about themselves, not God or their neighbors.

f.g: Yeast; normally excluded from offerings burned on the altar (Leviticus 2:11).

n: Now God lists warnings He already sent. First, famine — “clean teeth” because there was nothing to eat. Yet they did not come back to Him. This refrain repeats five times.

f.g: An ironic phrase for hunger: no food to dirty their teeth.

f.w: yet have ye not returned unto me

n: God held back the rain just before harvest, when it was needed most, and let it fall in one town but not another, so they could see His hand in it.
Thirsty people staggered from town to town looking for water but found too little. Still they did not return to God.
Crop diseases and locusts destroyed their gardens, vineyards, figs, and olives. Still they did not return.
Plague like the plagues of Egypt, and war that killed young men and left the stench of the dead in their camps. Still they did not return.
Some places were devastated like Sodom and Gomorrah; Israel was like a burning stick yanked from the fire. Even that close call did not turn them back.

f.w: a firebrand plucked out of the burning

n: Because every warning failed, a final encounter is coming: “Prepare to meet thy God.” In context a warning, these words also invite all of us to be ready to stand before God.
Amos describes the God they must meet: Creator of mountains and wind, who knows human thoughts and controls day and night. A hymn-like verse that magnifies His power.

f.w: declareth unto man what is his thought
f.g: Or reveals His own thoughts to man — through prophets (Amos 3:7).

f.w: The God of hosts, is his name
